Sugarcane.sowing_months: Autumn Oct-Nov; spring Feb-Mar; late spring Apr-May in western UP after wheat harvest; Bihar Jan-Feb (secondary source)
Sugarcane.peak_greenness_months: From AgriFieldNet data: median NDVI peak day 10 (~mid Oct). Standing crop, so NDVI stays flat through the rabi window.
Sugarcane.description: Long-duration standing crop planted in autumn or spring. Autumn-planted cane grows slowly in winter and rapidly in spring.
Sugarcane.distinguishing_cues: Flat NDVI like Fallow and Rice; radar (VV/VH) stays higher until about day 130 (early Feb) and then drops, unlike Fallow and Rice.

Garlic.sowing_months: Mid-Oct to mid-Nov recommended (Oct-Nov across north India and Bihar; Sep-Nov quoted for the northern plains)
Garlic.peak_greenness_months: From AgriFieldNet data: median NDVI peak day 130 (~early Feb)
Garlic.harvest_months: Roughly Mar-Apr (derived from Oct-Nov planting plus a 4-5 month crop duration from a secondary source; not directly sourced)
Garlic.description: Cool-season bulb crop planted in autumn and harvested when the tops start to yellow.
Garlic.distinguishing_cues: NDVI peak timing is close to Wheat, Gram and Lentil (peak day 130 vs 140). Cannot be separated from them by NDVI timing alone.

Potato.sowing_months: Oct-Nov in the Indo-Gangetic plains; early crop 3rd week Sep to 1st week Oct, main crop Oct, late crop 3rd week Oct to 1st week Nov; planting limit about 5 Nov in the eastern plains (Bihar, Odisha, eastern UP)
Potato.peak_greenness_months: From AgriFieldNet data: median NDVI peak day 100 (~early Jan)
Potato.harvest_months: Jan-Feb (secondary source); Jan-Mar for some varieties
Potato.description: Cool-season tuber crop grown in the plains from autumn planting to late winter harvest.
Potato.distinguishing_cues: Earlier and lower NDVI peak than Wheat and Mustard (data: peak day about 100, amplitude about 0.42 vs 0.61 for Wheat).

Rice.season: mainly kharif (Aman/Sali/Agahani winter rice, ~84% of rice); minor rabi/summer (Boro/Dalua/Garma) rice
Rice.sowing_months: Kharif: nursery Jun to 2nd week Jul (Odisha). Rabi/summer: sown Nov-Feb; Odisha dry-season nursery 15 Nov-15 Dec; Boro transplanted after 2nd week of Jan
Rice.peak_greenness_months: From AgriFieldNet data: median NDVI peak day 10 (~mid Oct), i.e. the tail of the kharif crop
Rice.harvest_months: Kharif: Oct-Dec (varies by variety and state). Rabi/summer: Mar-Jun
Rice.description: Dominant kharif crop in eastern India. Many fields are left fallow after the kharif harvest (rice-fallow), so the Oct-May window often shows little rice signal.
Rice.distinguishing_cues: NDVI is almost identical to Fallow in this window. Radar differs only slightly (VV dips deepest around day 160). Expect low confidence when Rice and Fallow are the top two candidates.
